locationallocation: Maximal Coverage Location-Allocation Using Geospatial Data

Source: R/locationallocation-package.R
locationallocation-package.Rd

locationallocation solves Maximal Coverage Location-Allocation (MCLA) problems with geospatial data: where to place new facilities so that as much (optionally weighted) demand as possible can reach a facility within a given travel time.

Workflow

  1. friction() retrieves a friction surface (time needed to cross each cell) from the Malaria Atlas Project, for walking or for the fastest mode of transport, at the spatial resolution of the analysis.

  2. traveltime() computes the travel time from any cell to the nearest existing facility. traveltime_stats() and traveltime_plot() summarize and map it.

  3. allocation() places new facilities anywhere within the area of interest (continuous problem), and allocation_discrete() selects them among candidate locations (discrete problem), until a target share of the demand is covered or a maximum number of facilities is reached. allocation_plot() maps the result.

Demand can be weighted by other layers (e.g., population times exposure to a hazard). The package includes example data for the city of Naples, Italy (naples_shape, naples_population, naples_fountains, naples_hot_days).

Algorithms

Travel times are least-cost paths over the friction surface. Both allocation problems are solved with a greedy heuristic that adds, at each step, the location covering the most demand not yet covered (Church & ReVelle, 1974), refined by vertex substitution (Teitz & Bart, 1968). See allocation() for details.

Online data

Friction surfaces are downloaded from the Malaria Atlas Project and, for the fastest mode at a fine resolution, road networks from OpenStreetMap. Downloads have fallbacks (cache, retries, mirrors) and can be cached on disk with cache = TRUE. See friction() for details and for the options that control this behavior.

References
